title: The logarithmic spiral is optimal for shoreline search: a computer-assisted proof
summary: A ship starts at a point of the plane and moves at unit speed; it has to reach an unknown straight line, of which neither the distance nor the direction is known. The competitive ratio of a path is the supremum, over all lines, of the time at which the line is reached divided by its distance. Baeza-Yates, Culberson and Rawlins conjectured that a logarithmic spiral, with ratio $C_{\mathrm{sp}} = 13.8111351794611\ldots$, is optimal. We give a computer-assisted proof.
